transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2025-06-10 15:00 PDT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Ava Martin (Redwood AE), Diego Lopez (Redwood SE), Sarah Chen (Orion Head of MLOps), Marcus Lee (Orion CTO), Priya Nair (Orion Procurement)

Summary (auto): POC must prove cost and latency economics for conversational summarization use case in production. Customer requests clear pilot credits and an acceptance checklist; procurement wants PO-based pilot or a short SOW.

[00:00] Ava: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm ava from redwood, i'll hand off to diego to run the tech bits but wanted to kick off with commercial ask — we know procurement is here so happy to walk through pilot guardrails
[00:22] Priya: hi, thanks — quick note from procurement side, for us pilots usually go via a PO up to $15k or a short term contract; we need clarity on scope and any overage billing
[00:35] Marcus: and hi from product — our main question is risk: latency and accuracy. we'll likely move to dedicated if numbers look good.
[00:48] Diego: great, i'll outline the benchmark plan in a bit. first could you confirm current traffic and expected workload?
[00:56] Sarah: sure — production day is roughly 50 rps at peak across our conversational summarization endpoint; average prompt is around 450 tokens, average generated summary ~150 tokens. monthly active users ~120k, monthly requests ~8 million (ballpark).
[01:18] Ava: perfect that's super helpful. so rough tokens per month = (450+150)*8M = ~4.8 billion tokens, ok that helps sizing. for a POC though we can run a representative subset to validate latency and cost.
[01:35] Marcus: target p95 latency for generation should be under 300ms; p50 under 120ms ideally. if we move to dedicated we want predictable latency for 99th percentile too.
[01:48] Diego: noted. for the POC we'll run both hosted and a dedicated-config mimic if you want; test will include: steady-state 50 rps, and a burst test to 150 rps to see autoscale behavior and tail latencies.
[02:05] Sarah: what about model choice and quantization? we use open models today but want a fair comparing baseline
[02:12] Diego: we'll bring a couple model variants — a medium open model quantized to int8 and a higher capacity fp16 variant to measure quality vs cost tradeoff. also measure KV cache hit rates for prefix-heavy flows; that tends to drop token cost a lot.
[02:30] Ava: on commercial guardrails — typical Redwood POC we offer 90-day pilot with credits, we can structure $10k core credit + optional $5k stretch credit if benchmarks hit acceptance. Pilot terms: usage caps, overage rates, list of deliverables (benchmark report, runbook, exportable logs).
[02:55] Priya: PO for $10k is straightforward. anything above needs legal review. can you send a simple SOW?
[03:03] Ava: yes we'll send a one-page SOW and the pilot T&Cs. overage rates are transparent — we'll propose an hourly token billing rate and a daily alert threshold to prevent surprises.
[03:15] Marcus: acceptance criteria — aside from latency we need no more than 5% quality regression on our labeled eval set vs current baseline. also we need end-to-end request success rate > 99.5%.
[03:32] Diego: we'll run quality evals against your labeled set you provide, and compute BLEU/ROUGE-ish metrics plus a small human spot check. we also track hallucination heuristics you may have.
[03:44] Sarah: data residency — some of our records are EU-sourced, we need logs kept in EU region and KMS integration with our key manager for at-rest encryption.
[03:55] Ava: Redwood Private / dedicated can meet that; for hosted we can pin region and integrate KMS for keys. we'll attach SOC 2 and encryption docs.
[04:08] Priya: timeline wise we need a quick turnaround — ideally pilot starts by June 23rd so it can complete ahead of Q3 planning. procurement approvals usually take two weeks after SOW/PO submission.
[04:20] Ava: that's doable. we'll aim to send SOW/PO template by Thursday (2025-06-12) and benchmark plan by Friday (2025-06-13).
[04:32] Diego: tech notes: benchmark will be two phases — phase 1 single-model latency/cost baseline (low concurrency), phase 2 stress and regression (load and quality). we'll instrument p50/p95/p99, cpu/gpu utilization, and KV cache hit/miss.
[04:50] Marcus: for dedicated capacity, what's the smallest commit? we want to understand path to reserved if pilot passes
[04:58] Ava: reserved capacity tiers start at a monthly commit equivalent to roughly 500k tokens/day sustained, but we can work on a short-term pilot extension and then convert credits into a committed discount if you sign a 12-month reserved capacity. we'll include examples in the pricing sheet.
[05:15] Sarah: can we get benchmark script access? we prefer running from our network to validate tail latency with our network path
[05:23] Diego: yes — we can provide a test harness and also run from Redwood side for parity. we'll provide both.
[05:31] Priya: will legal need a master subscription or just a pilot SOW?
[05:36] Ava: usually pilot via PO + SOW is enough; if it scales to Dedicated we do a contract with SLAs and security addendum. procurement can review SOW first.
[05:45] Marcus: any hidden fees we should watch for?
[05:48] Ava: no hidden fees — tokens, model variant selection, and optional data egress for private deployments if applicable. overage alerts prevent surprises.
[05:58] Sarah: on success criteria recap: p95 < 300ms, quality regression <5% vs baseline, >99.5% availability, cost per 1k tokens below x (we'll refine when we see benchmark).
[06:12] Ava: noted. we'll include an acceptance checklist in the SOW.
[06:18] Diego: tech caveat — model warmup and KV cache warm-up can impact early tail latencies; we'll run warmup traffic for 30 minutes before measuring steady-state.
[06:30] Marcus: sounds reasonable. what about data retention and logs for audits?
[06:36] Ava: logs retention is configurable; for Private we can keep logs in-customer region and lifecycle them per your policy. SOC 2 certification and audit logs are included in the enterprise package.
[06:48] Priya: please send the compliance packet and our security team will review.
[06:51] Ava: will attach SOC 2, encryption details, SSO/SAML guide and KMS integration notes.
[06:58] Sarah: ok next steps from our side: i will collate prompt set and anonymize records; priya will share procurement process; marcus will review acceptance criteria with product.
[07:10] Ava: great. any other concerns?
[07:14] Marcus: curious about fallback strategies — if hosted latency spikes do you have automatic model fallbacks to cheaper variants?
[07:22] Diego: yes, routing policies can fallback to a compatible variant or region; we can script canary rollouts and automatic fallback to maintain availability.
[07:30] Sarah: excellent. can you also include an example of what the benchmark report looks like?
[07:34] Ava: yes sample report will be included.
[07:36] Priya: timeline again — send SOW by 6/12, procurement will attempt PO by 6/20, aiming to start benchmarks week of 6/23.
[07:47] Ava: we'll align to that. thanks everyone.
[07:50] (crosstalk) everyone: thanks, bye.

End of call.
